title: HR Administrator
description:
HR Administrator

Guildford

30,000pa

Build Your Career in HR

We are looking for a highly organised, personable and proactive HR Administrator to join our growing business.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone at the beginning of their HR career who wants to gain broad, hands-on experience across the employee lifecycle and develop their skills within a fast-paced and supportive environment.

About the Role

You will provide day-to-day HR support across the business, working closely with employees and managers and supporting a wide range of HR activities, including:
- Maintaining accurate employee records and HR documentation
- Supporting recruitment from vacancy through to appointment
- Preparing and posting job advertisements and coordinating interviews
- Managing new starter onboarding and leaver administration
- Maintaining holiday, absence and probation records
- Coordinating staff rotas across multiple sites
- Supporting the monthly payroll process
- Maintaining training records and coordinating internal and external training
- Preparing HR letters, reports and documentation
- Supporting HR policies, procedures and compliance activities
- Acting as a first point of contact for general HR queries
- Supporting managers with employee reviews, training and HR processes
- Assisting with HR projects and continuous process improvements

What We're Looking For

You do not need extensive HR experience. We are looking for someone with the right attitude, strong organisational skills and a genuine interest in developing a career in HR.

Ideally, you will have:
- Previous experience in administration, HR, recruitment or another people-focused role
- Strong organisational and administrative skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- Confidence using Microsoft Office, particularly Word and Excel
- The ability to handle confidential information with discretion
- A proactive approach and the ability to take ownership of tasks
- A professional, approachable and reliable manner

A CIPD qualification, previous HR experience, payroll knowledge or recruitment experience would be advantageous, as would experience working within a professional or regulated environment.

Why Join Us?

This is more than an administration role. As you develop, there will be opportunities to take on increasing responsibility across employee relations, recruitment, performance management, training and HR projects.

For the right person, there is genuine potential to progress into an HR Advisor or HR Manager position as your experience and knowledge develop.

You will have the opportunity to make a real contribution to the development of people practices and HR processes within a growing organisation.

Equal Opportunities

We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds. All applicants will be considered based on their skills, experience, potential and suitability for the role.

If you are looking to start or develop your career in HR and want a role where you can learn, contribute and progress, we would love to hear from you.

title: HR Administrator
description:
HR Administrator

Farnham Temporary role ongoing

Are you an organised and proactive HR professional looking for a varied, hands-on role within a busy HR team?

Our client is seeking an HR Administrator to join their team in Farnham on a temporary basis for approximately three months. This role will focus on providing day-to-day HR administrative support, assisting with recruitment activities and responding to general employee queries.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous HR administration experience who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, has strong attention to detail and is confident supporting a range of HR processes.

The Role

As HR Administrator, you will provide essential administrative support across the HR function, helping to ensure the smooth running of day-to-day activities.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Supporting recruitment administration, including arranging interviews, liaising with candidates and preparing offer documentation
- Coordinating onboarding and induction processes for new starters
- Preparing employment contracts, offer letters and other HR documentation
- Responding to general HR queries from employees and managers
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date employee records and HR systems
- Supporting the administration of holidays, sickness absence and other employee changes
- Assisting with the preparation and maintenance of HR policies, procedures and employee documentation
- Ensuring personnel files and HR records are organised and compliant with data protection requirements

About You
- Previous experience in an HR administration or HR support role
- Good organisational skills and strong attention to detail
- Confident communication skills with a professional and approachable manner
- Comfortable handling confidential information
- Good IT skills, including experience using Microsoft Office and HR systems
- Able to manage competing priorities and work effectively in a busy environment
- A proactive, flexible approach and willingness to support the wider HR team

If you have previous HR administration experience and are available for a temporary assignment, we'd love to hear from you.

title: HR Coordinator
description:
People & Culture Coordinator
Hybrid working offered, great benefits and yearly bonus scheme
An excellent opportunity to join a fast-paced international business where the People & Culture team plays an important role in supporting employees through change, strengthening engagement and creating a positive employee experience.
Working closely with the People & Culture Business Partner, you ll provide coordination and administrative support across the employee lifecycle. Strong communication, organisation and attention to detail will be key to ensuring employees receive a supportive, consistent experience.

As People & Culture Coordinator you will be:
- Acting as a first point of contact for routine employee queries and escalating more complex matters when appropriate.
- Supporting employee engagement, recognition, wellbeing and culture initiatives.
- Coordinating onboarding and offboarding, including documentation and employee communications.
- Supporting compliance activity, reporting and the administration of People & Culture policies and processes.
- Providing administrative support for employee relations matters, including documentation, meeting coordination and follow-up.
- Carrying out and recording probation check-ins with employees and line managers.
- Coordinating absence management processes, maintaining records and supporting return-to-work activity.
- Supporting recruitment coordination, payroll and benefits administration as part of the wider employee lifecycle.

About You:
You ll have previous experience within HR, People & Culture or a related administrative role and be comfortable managing multiple priorities.
This is a great opportunity to develop broad People & Culture experience within a changing and evolving organisation. You ll have the chance to contribute to business transformation, support employees through change and continue to develop and progress your HR career.

title: Payroll Coordinator Immediate Start Temp to Perm
description:
Payroll Coordinator - Immediate Start

Location: Gatwick
Contract: Full-Time Temp to Perm
Salary: 20 - 23 per hour PAYE

4 days a week onsite and 1 from home.

We are partnering with a well-established and highly respected organisation to recruit an experienced Payroll Coordinator with HR duties. This is an excellent opportunity for a payroll professional with strong HR administration experience to join a busy and supportive team.

The successful candidate will play a key role in delivering an accurate and efficient payroll service, ensuring employees are paid correctly and on time while supporting a range of HR administrative activities. This role is heavily payroll-focused and would suit someone who enjoys working with numbers, legislation, benefits and employee data while maintaining a high level of accuracy and confidentiality.

Key Responsibilities
- Take ownership of the end-to-end monthly payroll process, ensuring all payroll inputs are processed accurately and within agreed deadlines.
- Maintain payroll records, including starters, leavers, salary changes, contractual amendments, absence information and benefit deductions.
- Act as the primary point of contact for employee payroll queries, resolving issues efficiently and providing excellent customer service.
- Administer pension schemes, employee benefits and salary sacrifice arrangements, ensuring accurate payroll deductions.
- Support payroll compliance activities, including statutory payments, tax codes, pension contributions and year-end processing.
- Assist with the preparation and administration of P11 D and PSA submissions, ensuring compliance with HMRC regulations and deadlines.
- Reconcile payroll reports and support the production of payroll-related data, management reports and audit information.
- Liaise with payroll providers and internal stakeholders to resolve discrepancies and improve payroll processes.
- Maintain HR and payroll systems, ensuring employee records remain accurate, up to date and compliant.
- Provide HR administrative support across the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, contractual documentation and employee record management.
- Support HR projects, reporting and general administration as required.

About You
- Proven experience in a payroll-focused position, processing payroll and handling payroll-related queries.
- Strong understanding of UK payroll legislation, statutory payments, pensions and payroll compliance requirements.
- Experience supporting P11 D, PSA and employee benefits administration.
- Previous experience using payroll systems such as ADP, Workday, SAP, Oracle or similar.
- Confident reconciling payroll data and producing payroll reports.
- Strong Excel skills, including working with large datasets, formulas and payroll reporting.
- Excellent attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
- Previous HR administration experience, ideally supporting employee lifecycle activities.
- Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

What's on Offer?
- Friendly and collaborative working environment.
- Hybrid working arrangements.
- Payroll-focused role with responsibility and autonomy.
- Opportunity to work within a well-established organisation and gain exposure to wider HR activities.
- Immediate start available.

If you are an experienced HR and Payroll professional looking for your next opportunity and enjoy delivering a high-quality service in a busy environment, we would love to hear from you.

title: People, Payroll & Compliance Officer
description:
An excellent opportunity has arisen for a highly organised and detail-focused administrator to join a respected educational organisation in Surrey. Working closely with the HR Manager, you will play a key role in supporting the delivery of efficient HR, payroll and workforce compliance processes.

Job Title: People, Payroll & Compliance Officer

Job Type: Permanent

Location: Surrey

Salary: £28,628 - £30,702 - 36 hours term time, plus 2 weeks - Office based

Benefits: Generous pension scheme, employee wellbeing support, professional development opportunities, generous holiday entitlement and access to a supportive working environment

Reference No: 16180

People, Payroll & Compliance Officer About the Role

This is a varied position that would suit an experienced HR, payroll or administrative professional who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities and ensuring high levels of accuracy. You will provide administrative support throughout the employee lifecycle, maintain workforce records and systems, coordinate payroll information and support a range of HR and compliance activities.

The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring employee data is accurate, confidential and up to date, while helping to maintain robust workforce compliance processes and supporting reporting requirements across the organisation. Main Responsibilities:
- Support all HR administration activities across the employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, contractual changes and leaver processes.
- Coordinate payroll information, processing changes accurately and liaising with payroll providers where required.
- Maintain employee records, HR systems and personnel files, ensuring information is accurate and up to date.
- Administer employee benefits, absence management systems and related documentation.
- Manage and respond to HR-related enquiries, ensuring a professional and timely service.
- Monitor and maintain workforce compliance records and documentation.
- Manage agency worker compliance tracking, ensuring all required checks and records are completed and maintained.
- Produce HR reports and workforce data to support management decision-making and statutory reporting requirements.
- Support organisational workforce census and reporting activities.
- Ensure compliance with GDPR, safeguarding requirements and internal policies.
- Assist with the continuous improvement of HR, payroll and compliance processes.
- Maintain confidentiality when handling sensitive employee and payroll information.

The Successful Candidate Will Have:
- Previous experience in an administrative, HR, payroll or compliance-focused role.
- Excellent organisational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
- Experience maintaining accurate records, databases, trackers and systems.
- The ability to manage multiple deadlines and prioritise workloads effectively.
- Strong IT skills, including experience using Microsoft Office applications and workforce systems.
- A professional and discreet approach when handling confidential information.
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to build positive working relationships with colleagues and external providers.
- An understanding of compliance processes, data protection and record-keeping requirements.
- A proactive and dependable approach with the ability to take ownership of administrative responsibilities.
- The ability to learn new systems and processes quickly.

Previous experience within HR, payroll or education would be advantageous, although candidates with strong administrative experience and a willingness to develop within a people-focused role are encouraged to apply. This is a fantastic opportunity for an organised and motivated professional to join a supportive organisation where attention to detail, teamwork and excellent service are highly valued.
